newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge orders payments in Lykes bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge orders payments in Lykes bankruptcy.

text.p: A U.S. judge overseeing the Lykes Bros. Steamship Co Inc bankruptcy case ordered that debts owed to Mitsui Engineering & Shipbuilding Co and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd be amoritized over 11 years, Lykes said on Thursday.

Lykes said in a news release that Chief Bankruptcy Judge Alexander Paskay had on Wednesday approved an agreement involving claims by the two companies, which will be paid an amount equal to $7,000 a day over 11 years.

Lykes said the agreement covers four large U.S.-flag containerships -- the M/V Stella Lykes, M/V Margaret Lykes, M/V Genevieve Lykes and the M/V Almeria Lykes -- used in Lykes' North Atlantic service.
Three of the vessels have been certified as essential to the national security of the United States, Lykes said.
"The four vessels will be time-chartered to a subsidiary to Canadian Pacific Ltd, which will purchase certain Lykes' operating assets," Lykes said.
The company said the judge's order had a brief time for creditors to comment before it becomes finalized.
